D1.reason_for_score: Score 3: N001 explicitly covers students using AI systems in University activities; N133 and N136 explicitly cover student use of GenAI software in any assessment task (prohibited unless written permission is granted by the Unit Coordinator), explicitly define prompting for editing/rewriting as GenAI use (N133 p.11 L044-L045), and explicitly address using GenAI for feedback before submission versus rewriting (N136 p.151 L021-L029).

D2.reason_for_score: Score 2: Decision-makers, criteria, and processes are documented for misconduct findings/appeals (Authorised Officer, Student Conduct Panel, Appeal Officer/SCAP under N141) and assessment mark appeals (Unit Coordinator, Head of School under N002 PC24). However, while the Unit Coordinator is named as the authority to grant written GenAI permission (N133, N136), the criteria and process for granting or refusing GenAI permission are not documented, and no review/appeal route is explicitly connected to a Unit Coordinator's GenAI permission decision.
D2.negative_search_or_access_note: No documented criteria or explicit appeal route found for a Unit Coordinator's decision to permit or refuse GenAI in a unit; general assessment/misconduct appeals and complaints routes (N002 PC24, N141, N144, N004) operate independently.

D3.reason_for_score: Score 1: Ambiguity/tension without a direct unresolved contradiction. N133 and N136 state a GenAI declaration 'must' be included when approved, whereas N134 and A005 frame declaring GenAI use as 'recommended' (unless GenAI-created content is included). Further, N136 p.149 prohibits GenAI without explicit written Unit Coordinator permission, yet N136 p.151 marks 'Using Gemini to provide feedback on your assessment task before you submit' as appropriate (green tick) without stating the Unit Coordinator permission condition, and N002 does not codify student GenAI rules and still cross-references the superseded Academic Misconduct Rules (p.44).

D4.reason_for_score: Score 2: Usable sequence for students (check Unit Outline/Blackboard for written Unit Coordinator permission; ask lecturer if unclear; retain drafts/process records/prompts; submit own work via LMS; include declaration after reference list). Material procedural details remain unclear for how a student formally requests permission if the Unit Outline is silent and whether a full prompt declaration is mandatory when AI is used only for formative planning/feedback with no verbatim text retained.
D4.negative_search_or_access_note: No formal application procedure or response timeframe found for requesting Unit Coordinator GenAI permission.

D5.reason_for_score: Score 2: Substantive protections cover student authorship (N002 own-work & Confirmation Checks; N136 Grammarly Authorship & Turnitin Clarity writing-process tracking), authorisation & disclosure (N133/N136 written Unit Coordinator permission, prompt/tool declaration, N141 misconduct enforcement), and equitable access (free Curtin Grammarly for all students; N002 P1 3.7; N214 reasonable adjustments; N231 disability accessibility GenAI exception). A material gap remains because student GenAI permission/declaration rules sit in webpages/guides rather than binding N002 procedures, N134/A005 soften declaration to 'recommended', and equitable access to non-Curtin persistent AI assistants is unaddressed.
D5.negative_search_or_access_note: Turnitin GenAI detection was disabled from 1 January 2026 (N134 p.13 L033-L035), shifting reliance to assessment design, Confirmation Checks, and process records.

D6.reason_for_score: Score 3: N001 establishes both periodic (annual rather than standard 5-year) and event-triggered review ('earlier if significant legislative changes occur', considering technological advances and emerging issues), assigns named ownership (Policy Manager: Provost; Policy Compliance Officer: Deputy Provost; Approval Authority: Senior Executive Team), and connects monitoring to revision via N014 Policy Development Procedures and N002 Unit Coordinator threat monitoring.
D6.negative_search_or_access_note: N001's scheduled review window (1 April 2026 - 30 June 2026) passed before the 2026-11-12 cut-off with no updated revision entry in the bundle, though operational updates occurred in 2026 (N134, N141).

case_summary.case_note: Outcome: Indeterminate with an incomplete pathway (Evidence=Sufficient, Critical gap=No, Mode=Prescribing, D1=3, D2=2, D3=1, D4=2, D5=2, D6=3, Review route=Yes). Curtin prohibits GenAI in any assessment task unless explicit written permission is granted by the Unit Coordinator (N133, N136) and requires the final submission to be the student's own work (N002, N133, N136), backed by Grammarly Authorship/Turnitin Clarity process tracking, prompt/tool declarations, Confirmation Checks, and Student Misconduct Rules 2026 (N141). Against Protocol v1.1 S1 ('Attributable student authorship and transparent, authorised AI assessment assistance'), there is no critical gap. Incomplete pathway stems from: (1) missing Unit Coordinator permission criteria/process and no explicit appeal link to GenAI permission decisions (D2=2, D4=2); (2) tension between mandatory declaration in N133/N136 vs 'recommended' in N134/A005 and N136 p.151's unmarked permission condition for pre-submission feedback (D3=1); and (3) student GenAI rules residing in guides/webpages rather than binding N002 procedures (D5=2).

human_review_flags: Confirm D3=1 vs D3=2 regarding tension between mandatory declaration ('must') in N133/N136 and 'recommended' in N134/A005, plus N136 p.151 green-tick feedback example.

Confirm D5=2 and Critical gap=No under Protocol v1.1 S1: verify whether placing student GenAI permission/declaration rules in N133/N136 rather than N002 creates a material gap or only an operational gap.
